approved_classes.ex:AminoAcid: Amino acid, any of a group of organic molecules that contains a basic amino group (−NH2), an acidic carboxyl group (−COOH), and an organic R group (or side chain) that's unique to every amino acid.
approved_classes.ex:EssentialAminoAcid: These are amino acids that are not produced by the body and must be obtained through food. They're also known as essential amino acids.
approved_classes.ex:SemiEssentialAminoAcid: Some amino acids are generated in the body, but production is insufficient; these amino acids are referred to as semi-essential amino acids.
approved_classes.ex:NonEssentialAminoAcid: Some amino acids are generated in the body and do not require supplementation; these amino acids are referred to as non-essential amino acids.
approved_classes.ex:AminoAcidClassificationBasedOnStructu: A classification of amino acids based on their structural characteristics. This includes aliphatic, hydroxyl group-containing, sulfur containing, acidic and amides, basic, aromatic, imino, heterocyclic.
approved_classes.ex:AminoAcidClassificationBasedOnPositio: A classification of amino acids based on the position of -NH2. This includes α-amino acid, β-amino acid, and γ-amino acid.
approved_classes.ex:AminoAcidClassificationBasedOnNutriti: A classification of amino acids based on their nutritional requirement. This includes essential amino acids (EAA), non-essential amino acids (NEAA), and semi-essential amino acids (SEAA).
approved_classes.ex:AminoAcidClassificationBasedOnMetabol: A classification of amino acids based on their metabolic fate. This includes purely ketogenic, ketogenic and glucogenic, and purely glucogenic.
approved_classes.ex:AminoAcidClassificationBasedOnPolarit: A classification of amino acids based on their polarity. This includes non-polar, polar with no charge on 'R' group, polar with positive 'R' group, and polar with negative 'R' group.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Glycine: Used to treat schizophrenia, stroke, sleep issues, BPH, metabolic syndrome, and a few uncommon inherited metabolic illnesses. Also used in the Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis method.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Alanine: Utilized to boost immunity and provide energy to the brain and central nervous system. Used in health supplements for muscle synthesis and maintenance, stress management, child growth, and immune system support.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Valine: Most commonly used in health supplements for its involvement in muscle synthesis and maintenance. Also supports stress management, child growth, and immune system support.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Leucine: Increases short-term physical performance or strength. Prevents muscle loss in various conditions including immobility. Helps lower blood glucose levels in type 2 diabetes.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Isoleucin: Required for children's optimal growth and maintaining nitrogen balance in adults. Also supports stress management, child growth, and immune system support.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Norleucin: Artificial amino acid used to research protein structure and function in the lab. Has a similar structure to Methionine.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Phenylala: Used to treat depression, inflammation, liver illness, muscle discomfort, weight loss, cholesterol reduction, and muscle development. Also used in the production of thyroid hormone.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Tyrosine: Commonly utilized in the production of thyroid hormone. Helps with mental performance, alertness, and memory. Used to treat depression, migraines, headaches, and anxiety.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Serine: Significant for brain and central nervous system function. Also used in the treatment of spinal spasticity, multiple sclerosis, familial spastic paraparesis, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Cysteine: Used to boost corticosteroid medication efficiency. Used in the treatment of surgery and trauma.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Threonine: Used to treat spinal spasticity, multiple sclerosis, familial spastic paraparesis, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Methionin: Used to prevent and cure depression, inflammation, liver illness, muscle discomfort. Also used in the treatment of weight loss, cholesterol reduction, and muscle development.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Iodogorgi: A type of medicine used to help people reduce weight, lower cholesterol, and develop muscle. Also known as Diiodothyronine.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Thyroxine: Used to treat thyroid underactivity (hypothyroidism). Replaces or increases the amount of thyroid hormone generated by the thyroid gland.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Tryptopha: Used to treat anxiety and depression. Also used in the treatment of migraines, headaches, and to boost growth hormone production.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Proline: Used to improve joint and skin health. May also help with muscle development and injury healing.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Hydroxypr: Required for the formation of collagen, the body's principal structural protein. Also used in the treatment of acne, photoaging, dry skin, psoriasis, melasma, fibromyalgia, dental scaling, and dry mouth.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#AsparticA: Used to treat stress and exhaustion. Aids in the generation of energy from carbohydrates as well as RNA and DNA production.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Asparagin: Necessary for brain development and function. Also used in the treatment of fibromyalgia, dental scaling, dry mouth, and prevention/treatment of urinary tract stones.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#GlutamicA: Serves as a source of energy for the brain. Improves brain clarity, mental alertness, and mood. Used to treat Parkinson's disease, fatigue, and schizophrenia.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Beta-Hydr: Used in the treatment of acne, photoaging, dry skin, psoriasis, melasma, fibromyalgia, dental scaling, and dry mouth. Also studied for prevention/treatment of urinary tract stones.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Glutamine: Used to maintain blood sugar levels. Supports sports and performance in health supplements. Also used to support liver function and wound healing.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Arginine: Non-essential amino acid with antiatherogenic, anti-ischemic, antiplatelet, and antithrombotic effects. Plays a role in the treatment of cardiovascular disease.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Lysine: Minimizes cold sores when taken orally or applied as a cream. Used to treat anemia and reduce blood pressure. Also used in baby feeding.
approved_classes.http://example.org/amino_acids#Histidine: Used to treat anemia, reduce blood pressure, and support infant feeding. Also used in the production of hemoglobin.

ex:isMadeUpOf.comment: Protein is made up of amino acids, which are the building blocks of the molecule.

ex:hasFunctionalGroup.comment: The amino ( -NH2) group is basic, whereas the carboxyl ( -COOH) group is acidic.

ex:hasRGroup.comment: The remaining two bonds of the α-carbon atom are generally satisfied by a hydrogen (H) atom and the R group [1–6, 9].

ex:isSolubleIn.comment: Most of the amino acids are usually soluble in water and insoluble in organic solvents.

ex:meltsAt.comment: Amino acids are generally melted at a higher temperature often above 2000 C.

ex:tastes.comment: Taste: Amino acids are also sweet (Glycine, Alanine and Valine), tasteless (Leucine) or Bitter (Arginine & Isoleucine).

ex:hasOpticalIsomer.comment: All amino acids except glycine possess optical isomers because of the presence of asymmetric α-carbon atoms and show optical activity.

ex:hasZwitterion.comment: The name zwitter is derived from the German word which implies hybrid. Zwitter ion (or) dipolar ion is a hybrid molecule containing positive & negatively ionic groups.

ex:hasIsoelectricPoint.comment: The proton shifts from the carboxyl group to the amino group of the self-molecule at normal pH cellular levels.

ex:undergoesDecarboxylation.comment: The amino acids will undergo alpha Decarboxylation to make the corresponding amines. Histidine → Histamine + CO2 Tyrosine → Tyramine + CO2 Tryptophan → Tryptamine + CO2

ex:reactsWithAlkalies.comment: Amino acids react with alkalies to make Salts.

ex:reactsWithAlcohols.comment: Amino acids are reacted with an alcohol to form, Ester.

ex:reactsWithAmmonia.comment: The carboxyl group of dicarboxylic amino acids reacts with NH3 to form Amides. Aspartic acid + NH3→ Asparagine Glutamic acid + NH3→Glutamine

ex:reactsWithMineralAcids.comment: When the amino acids are treated with mineral acids (like HCl), it forms Acid Salts.

ex:hasNinhydrinReaction.comment: When Amino acids (or) Imino acid react with Ninhydrin molecule it gives Color. When it gives Purple color (Ruhemanns Complex) the Unknown sample is Amino acids (Which have primary amine NH2) or it gives Yellow color the Unknown sample is Imino acid (-NH-).

ex:isLOrD.comment: Only L-amino acids are manufactured in cells and incorporated into proteins. Some D -amino acids are found within the cell walls of bacteria, but not in bacterial proteins.

ex:isEssential.comment: Eight amino acids are very important for humans. E.g. Valine, Leucine, Isoleucine, Threonine, Methionine, Phenylalanine, Tryptophan, and Lysine.

ex:isSemiEssential.comment: Some amino acids are generated in the body, but production is insufficient; these amino acids are referred to as semi-essential amino acids.

ex:isNonEssential.comment: Some amino acids are generated in the body and do not require supplementation; these amino acids are referred to as non-essential amino acids.

ex:isClassifiedBasedOnStructure.comment: Indicates the classification of an amino acid based on its structural characteristics.

ex:isClassifiedBasedOnPositionOfNH2.comment: Indicates the classification of an amino acid based on the position of -NH2.

ex:isClassifiedBasedOnNutritionalRequire.comment: Indicates the classification of an amino acid based on its nutritional requirement.

ex:isClassifiedBasedOnMetabolicFate.comment: Indicates the classification of an amino acid based on its metabolic fate.

ex:isClassifiedBasedOnPolarity.comment: Indicates the classification of an amino acid based on its polarity.

canonical_terms.aliphaticAminoAcids: The naturally occurring amino acids are in α-L-amino acids, which include alanine, leucine, isoleucine, valine, and methionine.
canonical_terms.hydroxylGroupContainingAminoAcids: Serine, threonine, and tyrosine have hydroxyl groups. Tyrosine can also be classified as an aromatic amino acid due to its aromatic character.
canonical_terms.sulfurContainingAminoAcids: Cysteine with a sulfohydryl group and methionine with a thioether group are the two amino acids absorbed during protein synthesis.
canonical_terms.acidicAminoAcidsAndTheirAmides: Aspartic acid and glutamic acids are dicarboxylic monoamino acids, while asparagine and glutamine are their respective amide derivatives.
canonical_terms.basicAminoAcids: Lysine, arginine (with guanidino group), and histidine (with imidazole ring) are dibasic monocarboxylic acids. They are highly basic in character.
canonical_terms.aromaticAminoAcids: Phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan have an indole ring. Histidine may also fall under this category.
canonical_terms.iminoAminoAcid: Proline is a unique amino acid with a Pyrrolidine ring instead of the amino group (-NH2) found in other amino acids; it possesses an imino group (=NH).
canonical_terms.heterocyclicAminoAcids: Histidine, tryptophan, and proline are heterocyclic amino acids.
canonical_terms.alphaAminoAcid: The amino group attached to the next carbon of the carboxyl group is called α-amino acid. All naturally occurring amino acids are in α-L-amino acids.
canonical_terms.betaAminoAcid: β-amino acid refers to the amino group attached to the third carbon (numbering from the Carboxyl group) of an amino acid, such as -alanine.
canonical_terms.gammaAminoAcid: γ-amino acid refers to the amino group connected to the fourth carbon (numbering from the Carboxyl group), like GABA (Gamma Amino Butyric Acid).
canonical_terms.essentialAminoAcids: Methionine, Arginine, Tryptophan, Valine, Isoleucine, Leucine, Phenylalanine, and Lysine are essential for the individual's appropriate development and maintenance.
canonical_terms.nonEssentialAminoAcids: Glycine, Alanine, Serine, Cysteine, Aspargine, Aspartic acid, Glutamic acid, Glutamine, Tyrosine, and Proline can be synthesized by the body to meet biological demands.
canonical_terms.semiEssentialAminoAcids: Histidine and Arginine are semi-essential. They are required in the diet of growing children but not for mature individuals.
canonical_terms.purelyKetogenicAminoAcids: Leucine and Lysine can be used to make fat, as they are completely ketogenic.
canonical_terms.ketogenicAndGlucogenicAminoAcids: Lysine, Isoleucine, Phenylalanine, Tyrosine & Tryptophan partially enter the ketogenic pathway during metabolism while entering the glucogenic pathway.
canonical_terms.purelyGlucogenicAminoAcids: The remaining 14 amino acids are fully glucogenic and can be used as a starting point for glucose or glycogen production.
canonical_terms.nonPolarAminoAcids: Alanine, Leucine, Isoleucine, Valine, Methionine, Phenylalanine, Tryptophan, and Proline are hydrophobic (water-hating) with no charge on the 'R' group.
canonical_terms.polarAminoAcidsWithNoChargeOnRG: Glycine, Serine, Threonine, Cysteine, Glutamine, Asparagine, and Tyrosine have uncharged R groups but contribute to protein structure hydrogen bonding.
canonical_terms.polarAminoAcidsWithPositiveRG: Lysine, Arginine, and Histidine are polar with positive 'R' group.
canonical_terms.polarAminoAcidsWithNegativeRG: Aspartic acid and Glutamic acid are aromatic dicarboxylic monoamino acids with negative 'R' groups.
